venezuela.title: Flag of the Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela

colors.note: Top band; represents the wealth of the land and its resources.
Middle band; represents the Caribbean Sea separating Venezuela from Spain.
Bottom band; represents the blood shed in the struggle for independence.
The eight stars in an arc on the blue band; symbolise the original provinces that signed the Act of Independence.

desc:
- A horizontal tricolour of yellow, blue, and red with an arc of eight white five-pointed stars on the blue band
- The state flag adds the national coat of arms in the upper hoist corner
- Designed by Francisco de Miranda in 1806 and updated in 2006 to add an eighth star representing Guayana province
trivia:
- The flag is shared in colour order with Colombia and Ecuador, all of which descend from Gran Colombia
- The eighth star was added in 2006 by President Hugo Chavez, honouring Simon Bolivar's 1817 decree to include Guayana
- The original seven-star version, designed by Francisco de Miranda, dates from 1806 and is among the oldest independence banners in the Americas

venezuela-state-flag.title: State flag of Venezuela

colors.note: Middle band with eight white stars.

desc:
- The state (or 'government') flag is the civil tricolour with the national coat of arms added in the upper hoist corner
- Flown by government bodies, embassies, naval vessels, and the armed forces; the civil flag (without CoA) is the version most commonly seen in public
- Wikipedia lists the civil version as the national flag; the state flag is a restricted-use variant
